proof_summary: After clearing the factorial denominator, the proof rules out composite moduli by comparing \(p\)-adic valuations: multiples of \(\operatorname{ord}_p(2)\) among the exponents (with an extra contribution from \(2^{p\operatorname{ord}_p(2)}-1\)) force more divisibility than the factorial can have, while powers of two are excluded by an exact \(2\)-adic calculation. Once primality is known, a nonmaximal order \(d<n-1\) would make the prime divide the factor \(2^d-1\) in the product, and the assumed congruence would then force it to divide \((n-1)!\), a contradiction.
